findings.title: tests/home.spec.ts is an 822-line spec covering 14 concerns
findings.evidence: home.spec.ts is 822 LOC with 42 tests and 35 page.goto('/') calls, mixing hero, nav, theme toggle, mobile menu, stories, pointer preview, no-JS, 404, reduced motion, scroll spy, CSP (reads dist/_headers with fs, 725-740), perf budget, colophon, placeholder guard and shortcuts. Section banners are out of order (7 after 404, then 8b, then unnumbered).
findings.suggested_approach: Split by concern: nav.spec.ts, theme.spec.ts, stories.spec.ts, preview.spec.ts, shortcuts.spec.ts, build-output.spec.ts (CSP, placeholder, budget, colophon). Share goto and locators through a fixture or tests/helpers.ts.
findings.success_metric: No spec file over 250 LOC; playwright --list count identical before and after.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove equal with npx playwright test --list before and after (same test count and titles; the colophon renders this count).

findings.title: initPreview is a 220-line closure with 12 shared mutable variables
findings.evidence: initPreview spans 220-439 (220 LOC) and holds 12 mutable closure variables (ratio, tx, x, y, raf, then, shown, row, side, want, showing, roomH) shared by sizeFor, resize, room, tab, top, fits, pickSide, target, tick, swap (complexity 15, 34 lines), show, hide. Placement maths (sizeFor/fits/pickSide/target) reads DOM rects inline so it cannot be unit tested.
findings.suggested_approach: Extract the pure placement maths (sizeFor, fits, pickSide, target) into peek-layout.ts taking explicit {rect, viewport, navBottom, tabH, roomH} inputs; keep the pointer/raf/swap shell in preview.ts and group the mutable lets into one state object. Keep PEEK_* constants next to the layout module.
findings.success_metric: initPreview under 120 LOC; placement functions take no closed-over mutable state; swap complexity under 8.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove with the three 'pointer preview' specs in home.spec.ts (327-378) plus npm run build.

findings.title: ThemeToggle press() is 103 lines with five jobs
findings.evidence: press (322-424) is 103 LOC, complexity 11, mixing five jobs: reduced-motion and double-tap gating, class mode switching, geometry, DOM creation of ring/canvas/clip style, and the rAF clip loop; the enclosing initThemeToggle script is 230 LOC. ring, clip and frameAt are nullable temporaries assigned inside the startViewTransition callback and re-cast at 396-398 (as HTMLElement | null). The dissolve frame builder (284, complexity 22) nests three loops.
findings.suggested_approach: Extract createRing(x, y, grow) returning {ring, clip, frameAt}, runDissolve(t, parts, from, to) for the ready.then body, and a pure squareRuns(w, h, r, grow) that returns rect parts; move the script to src/scripts/theme-toggle.ts imported by the component. No casts needed once createRing returns a typed object.
findings.success_metric: press under 40 LOC; no 'as ... | null' casts in the file; frame builder complexity under 12.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove with the four theme specs (home.spec.ts 71-149) and screenshot compare of mid-dissolve frames.

findings.title: initStories is a 239-line function mixing six concerns
findings.evidence: initStories spans lines 452-690 (239 LOC) and mixes six concerns: history push/pop state, opener focus return, pull-to-close, swipe between stories, dismiss animation, popstate handling; module-level mutable current/opener at 458-459.
findings.suggested_approach: Split into a stories module with showStory/closeStory plus separate gesture (pull-to-close, swipe) and history helpers sharing one small state object.
findings.success_metric: No function in the stories code exceeds 60 LOC; story specs in home.spec.ts and media.spec.ts pass unchanged.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove equivalence with the story tests in tests/home.spec.ts and tests/media.spec.ts plus a dist/ diff (markup must not change).

findings.title: Clipped-border test holds a 36-line in-page loop (complexity 14)
findings.evidence: The clipped-border test (568-616) holds a 36-line in-page loop (complexity 14, nested for/some/for with break), inline in the test body and generated for two widths; it is the highest-complexity function in the repo.
findings.suggested_approach: Move the evaluate body to tests/helpers/clipped-frames.ts exporting findClippedFrames(page); the test becomes setViewport, goto, wait for in, expect(await findClippedFrames(page)).toEqual([]).
findings.success_metric: Test body under 12 LOC; helper holds the loop.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove with a seeded regression (temporary overflow:hidden on a parent of a framed element) failing identically before and after.

findings.title: media.spec.ts viewport test is 74 lines nested 6 deep
findings.evidence: The 'media stays within the viewport' test (102-177) is 74 LOC, complexity 7, nested to depth 6 (width, reducedMotion, theme, if reduce, if chromium, image) and mixes assertions with artifact capture (testInfo.attach of layout JSON and a full-page JPEG, 149-172). The same image-decoded poll appears twice (77-84, 139-146).
findings.suggested_approach: Extract waitForImagesLoaded(page) and attachLayoutEvidence(page, testInfo, width, theme); keep the loops but call the helpers.
findings.success_metric: No nesting deeper than 3; the image-loaded poll defined once.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove with playwright --list equality and the attachments still produced on chromium.

findings.title: Shortcut keydown handler has cyclomatic complexity 16
findings.evidence: The document keydown listener in initShortcuts (1084-1112) has cyclomatic complexity 16 (lizard worst function in the repo): modifier/repeat guard, editable-target guard, open-dialog guard, ?, Escape, shortcutsOn, t, JUMPS lookup with scroll-or-navigate branch.
findings.suggested_approach: Extract an isIgnorableKey(e) guard and a key-to-action table ({'?': toggleCard, t: clickTheme, ...JUMPS}) so the listener is a guard plus one lookup.
findings.success_metric: Listener complexity drops to 5 or less in lizard; keyboard shortcut specs pass unchanged.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove equivalence with the keyboard-shortcut tests in tests/home.spec.ts.

findings.title: home-interactions.ts is a 1152-line god file with 14 unrelated behaviours

Shared state is the module-level teardowns, reduce, greeted. BaseLayout.astro:88 imports only init().
findings.suggested_approach: Split into src/scripts/home/ with dom.ts (listen, teardowns, cleanup, reduce, fineHover), reveal.ts (reveal, stagger, imageFade), nav.ts (scrollSpy, scrolledNav, mobileNav), preview.ts, stories.ts, hover-finds.ts (brush, flip, hop, typeChip), shortcuts.ts; keep home-interactions.ts as the thin init() that calls each in the current order. Move code verbatim, no logic edits.
findings.success_metric: home-interactions.ts under 80 LOC (init only); no extracted module over 300 LOC; init() call order unchanged.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove equivalence with npm run build, then npm test (home.spec.ts stories, preview, nav, shortcuts specs), and diff dist/ HTML (script bundle hash will change, markup must not).

findings.title: colophon.astro spawns Playwright during the static build

It couples the page build to the Playwright install and spec files, and starts a second Playwright process in every npm run build. Prose in the same file (146-148) hard-codes the 350 KiB and 1.5 MiB budgets the specs enforce.
findings.suggested_approach: Move the listing into src/lib/test-count.ts (one exported function, typed JSON shape) so the page imports a number; take budget figures from one constant in src/data/colophon.ts shared by prose and stats.
findings.success_metric: colophon.astro frontmatter under 15 LOC; budgets defined once; dist/colophon/index.html identical.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove with npm run build and a byte diff of dist/colophon/index.html.

findings.title: One script queries markup owned by ten components with no shared selector constants
findings.evidence: one 1152-line script drives ~14 behaviours and queries markup owned by Nav, Work, ProjectRow, ProjectStory, Hero, About, Contact, Numbers, MediaFrame, ThemeToggle by class/id/data-attr (see home_interactions_coupling, 25 selectors from lines 35-1101); renaming a class in a component silently breaks the script (no shared constant or type) Confirmed at file:line by grep.
findings.suggested_approach: One shared selectors module (class, id and data-attr names) imported by home-interactions.ts and referenced from components, so renames fail at type level; then split init* into per-behaviour modules under src/scripts/.
findings.success_metric: home-interactions.ts has 0 literal selectors outside the shared module; file under 400 LOC; Playwright specs unchanged and passing.
findings.equivalence_proof: Equivalence proof: npm run build then diff dist/ (HTML identical, JS only differs by moved code); astro check 0 errors; Playwright home.spec.ts covering it.

findings.title: initFlip physics and Hero.astro CSS share an undocumented contract with no test
findings.evidence: initFlip (768-879) is a physics state machine (FLIP table, tick, push, stop, right, back) with 11 closure lets (th, w, caught, running, last, dir, spun, prev, rightTimer, back). Its contract with Hero.astro (--flip, --flip-s, --flip-m, .turned, .brushing) lives only in the comment at 738-750, so a Hero CSS edit and the TS change together. Neither tests/home.spec.ts nor tests/media.spec.ts mentions data-flip, data-brush or data-type (grep found none), so this code has no safety net.
findings.suggested_approach: Add a Playwright spec first (click the hero label, expect settled --flip of none or rotateX(180deg)), then pull the integrator into a pure step(state, dt, FLIP) function and return {flip, flipS, flipM, turned} for one apply() that writes the DOM.
findings.success_metric: initFlip under 60 LOC; step() has no DOM access; a spec asserts the settled --flip value after a click.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove with the new spec plus a screenshot compare of the hero label at rest.

findings.title: Build identity (git lookups) resolved in Footer and colophon frontmatter
findings.evidence: resolveCommit (10-22) and describeCommit (28-48) run git via execSync in the Footer frontmatter, so every page rendering Footer (via BaseLayout) re-executes git rev-parse and git log; describeCommit interpolates the sha into a shell string (git log -1 ... ${sha}) rather than passing args. Build identity logic lives in a presentation component. Same pattern: src/components/Footer.astro:3 and src/pages/colophon.astro:2 both import node:child_process, so git state couples rendering in two places. (B2 build-time-shell-in-frontmatter merged here.)
findings.suggested_approach: Move to src/lib/build-info.ts exporting a memoised getBuildInfo() using execFileSync with an args array; Footer destructures it.
findings.success_metric: Footer frontmatter under 10 LOC; git invoked once per build.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove with npm run build and a diff of the footer HTML in dist/ (same commit when run in the same checkout).

findings.title: Literal colours in Footer.astro instead of tokens

findings.suggested_approach: Replace each literal with an existing token only where the resolved value is identical, or color-mix on a token that resolves to the same value. A literal with no identical token is a visual change and belongs under sign-off.
findings.success_metric: No UI colour literals outside tokens.css in this file.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove with npm run build and light and dark screenshots of the component before and after.

findings.title: ThemeToggle holds module state and a never-removed listener, coupled to the T shortcut by a synthetic click
findings.evidence: current and lastClick (248-249) are mutable state shared by press and a document-level click listener (428-437) that is never removed, while home-interactions.ts has a listen/teardowns discipline so init() is re-runnable. The T shortcut drives the toggle by a synthetic click (home-interactions.ts:1101 getElementById('theme-toggle')?.click()), coupling two scripts through the DOM.
findings.suggested_approach: Move the logic into the shared scripts module, register via the same listen() so init() can clean it, and have the T shortcut call an exported toggleTheme(originEl).
findings.success_metric: All listeners registered through listen(); the T shortcut calls a function, not element.click().
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove with 'T switches the theme' and the keyboard/mid-switch theme specs (home.spec.ts 106-149, 746).

A major bump can change build output, formatting or compiler diagnostics, so it is not behaviour-preserving by default.
findings.suggested_approach: One pass per package, only when the owner asks. For each: bump, npm run build, astro check, dist/ diff, full suite. typescript 7 also needs a tsc strict re-run to see how the 19 known strict errors change.
findings.success_metric: Each package at latest major with build and tests green.
findings.equivalence_proof: npm run build and astro check unchanged; the relevant spec passes unchanged.

findings.title: Brittle waits and fixed-pixel input in the Playwright specs
findings.evidence: Fixed sleeps: waitForTimeout(200) at tests/home.spec.ts:141, (1000) at :577 ('let the headline lines finish rising'), (300) at :765 (proves a key does nothing), (1500) at :806 (proves nothing loops). Fixed-pixel input: mouse.click(300, 800) at :194, mouse.click(5, 5) at :260, mouse.move(1400, 880) at :818. Size-sensitive waits and budgets: waitUntil networkidle at tests/home.spec.ts:683 (350 KiB transfer budget) and tests/media.spec.ts:66, :91. Each is time-based or layout-coupled, slows every run and can flake on a loaded runner. (B1 magic-waits and B2 brittle-tests reported the same file; merged.)
findings.suggested_approach: 141: keep (the spacing is the test input). 577: wait on the headline animations finishing via document.getAnimations(). 765: assert the stored 'shortcuts' value instead of sleeping. 806: poll getAnimations() empty over a bounded window. Replace fixed-pixel clicks with locator clicks; keep the size budgets and the networkidle waits where the byte count is the assertion.
findings.success_metric: waitForTimeout remains only where the delay is the test input; suite green with --repeat-each=3.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove by running the suite on 3 engines with --repeat-each=3.

findings.title: media.spec.ts first test is 51 lines of unrelated assertions
findings.evidence: The first test (4-55) is 51 lines of unrelated assertions (peek attribute, 7 story ids, alt regexes, copy strings, mascot absence, banned-phrase regex), so the first failure hides the rest; budgets 350*1024 and 1.5*1024*1024 are inline (69, 93).
findings.suggested_approach: Split into per-concern tests (peek data, alt text, copy and forbidden phrases) sharing a beforeEach goto; name the budgets in the shared fixtures module.
findings.success_metric: First test split into 3 tests under 20 LOC each; budgets are named constants.
findings.equivalence_proof: Prove with a full suite run.
